questions.question_text: The business expert assigned to the project tells you that an account may be reported on more than one statement. Does the model correctly depict that and why?

answers.text: Yes, because the 0..* into Statement means an account may not be reported.
answers.explanation: True, the 0..* means an account may not be reported at all. But the "*" means it could be on multiple statements, so this is not the correct answer. BABOK Figure 10.15.2

answers.text: No, because the 1..* coming out of Account means an account may be reported on one statement.
answers.explanation: No, the diagram does not limit the number of statements to one. The * means many. The "1..* coming out" is actually going into the Account. BABOK Figure 10.15.2

answers.text: Yes, because the 1..* coming out of Account means an account may be reported on one or more statements.
answers.explanation: The "1..*" means a statement may consist of one or more accounts. BABOK Figure 10.15.2

answers.text: Yes, because the 0..* into Statement means an account may be reported on zero or many statements.
answers.explanation: The 0..* means an account may appear on zero to many statements. It is a convention of class diagrams. BABOK Figure 10.15.2

answers.text: Another type of model would be the one to dictate how often statements are produced.

questions.question_text: Lexi is communicating business analysis information to resource managers via email every Monday as per the stakeholder engagement approach. Lexi is frequently contacted by several of those same resource managers asking her about information that was already emailed. What should Lexi do to resolve this breakdown in communication?

answers.text: Refer the resource managers to the email.
answers.explanation: This course of action may be tempting but it's not the guidance suggested in the BABOK which is to engage the stakeholders to ensure they understand the information being communicated and that email is even an effective mode of communication

answers.text: Lexie needs to engage stakeholders to ensure they understand the information being communicated and that email is an effective mode of communication.
answers.explanation: This response is aligned to BABOK guidance

answers.text: Begin scheduling weekly conference calls to provide a forum for follow-up discussion.
answers.explanation: This may end up being a viable alternative to the emails, but at this point may result in redundant work. The guidance the BABOK offers would be to engage the stakeholders to ensure they understand the information being communicated and that email is even an effective mode of communication

answers.text: Replace the emails with weekly meetings with minutes that can be referenced after the meeting.
answers.explanation: Emails may eventually be replaced with another communication modality, but at this point this course of action may be a bit premature. The guidance the BABOK offers would be to engage the stakeholders to ensure they understand the information being communicated and that email is even an effective mode of communication

questions.question_text: Jax is a BA interviewing a client regarding business rules related to discounts for car insurance. The customer started relating several "If, then" scenarios. For example, "If their age is 16-25, no discount. If their age is 26-35 and they have been accident free for a minimum of 3 years, they will receive a 5% discount. But, if they have other policies with us, they will receive an 8% discount. If they are from 36-50 years old and...." Jax was writing furiously trying to keep up! answers.explanation: This would not be an effective decision model given the scenario as this diagram is best used for complex decisions requiring knowledge sources.

This is partially correct but there is another response that describes the type of decision model that would answer the question and is a better answer.

questions.question_text: Given important stakeholders in this organization are family members, what do you need to do differently to define their roles and responsibilities?

answers.text: Nothing. You should identify the family members (and their characteristics) who will be impacted by the change as you normally would.
answers.explanation: It may require a bit more tact when defining roles and responsibilities in a family-run organization. This answer is essentially the definition of stakeholder analysis, an important element in planning stakeholder engagement and partially correct. The BABOK says “Stakeholder analysis involves identifying the stakeholders (who will be directly or indirectly impacted by the change)”

answers.text: Understand that despite the titles family members have, the parents will have ultimate decision-making authority.
answers.explanation: This is a false assumption. It may be true in some family-run organizations, but it is still an assumption. It would be better to conduct stakeholder analysis to clarify assumptions.

answers.text: Use a Roles and Permission Matrix for this effort.
answers.explanation: This type of technique does help define roles. But it only refers to who can Create-Read-Update-Delete (CRUD) data and other resources. It surprisingly is only referenced in task 8.4, Assess Enterprise Limitations and is too solution-focused to apply here

answers.text: Nothing. You should find an organizational chart to consider any unique needs.
answers.explanation: It may require a bit more tact when defining roles and responsibilities in a family-run organization. But using a technique such as organizational modeling works for a family business as well as for any other organization. However, there is nothing in the case study to indicate an organizational chart exists, making it a good distractor (and partially correct). The BABOK spells out that it is used “to determine if the organizational units or people listed have any unique needs and interests that should be considered.”

questions.question_text: You feel strongly about continuously improving your business analysis efforts. When you identify potential improvements, which of the following roles is the most important one to consult with and why?

answers.text: Shelly and Stan, the sponsors, since they will have to approve any additional funding needed.

answers.text: Project Manager, since any potential corrections will impact the project’s schedule and budget.
answers.explanation: All the possible answers in this question are potential stakeholders involved with business analysis performance improvements. But because of the effect on the project, the PM is the best choice. “If potential problems or opportunities for improvement are identified, the project manager must be consulted before changes are implemented to assess whether those changes will have an impact on the project.”

answers.text: Chis, a key Subject Matter Expert, to set expectations regarding his involvement.
answers.explanation: True, Domain Subject Matter experts play a role in business analysis performance improvements. Chris appears to be a Domain SME, one of the listed stakeholders for business analysis performance improvements. But like the answer for the sponsors, the PM is the better choice

answers.text: Garrett, the assumed CIO and a key Subject Matter Expert, since any improvements will affect IT.
answers.explanation: True, Domain Subject Matter experts play a role in business analysis performance improvements. It could be argued that Garrett is more of an Implementation Subject Matter Expert. Plus, not all improvements would involve IT
